questions.prompt: Explain how the board makes a status change atomic, walking through the transact function and what each of its guards prevents.

keyPoints.text: A status change writes the new state, an audit entry and follower notifications, which must commit together or not at all.
keyPoints.quote: Atomicity means those changes commit together or none do.

keyPoints.text: BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock before the document is read, so two processes cannot both read and then both write.
The callback must be synchronous; an async callback would resolve after COMMIT, so a returned Promise is rejected.
keyPoints.quote: is exactly the bug the explicit `instanceof Promise` check prevents

keyPoints.text: validateDatabase runs on the whole aggregate before writing, so a dangling reference cannot commit.
keyPoints.quote: so a command that leaves a dangling reference cannot commit

keyPoints.text: The catch rolls back, so a mid-change failure leaves neither the status, its audit nor its notifications behind.
keyPoints.quote: leaves neither the status nor its audit nor its notifications behind

keyPoints.text: The whole mechanism is one function in the store.

questions.prompt: Why does the board need optimistic concurrency even though writes are serialized, and where exactly must the version check run?

keyPoints.text: Optimistic concurrency solves a different problem from atomicity.
keyPoints.quote: Optimistic concurrency addresses a different problem.

keyPoints.text: Two editors can both read the same version before either transaction starts.
keyPoints.quote: Alice and Bob can both read version 3 before either starts a transaction.

keyPoints.text: Serializing writes alone cannot tell that Bob edited stale content.
keyPoints.quote: Serializing database writes alone would not detect that Bob edited stale content.

keyPoints.text: The form keeps the version it originally read, and the service compares it with the current record.
keyPoints.quote: the form retains the version it originally read

keyPoints.text: The comparison runs inside the transaction on the record as it is now, not on the rendered copy.
keyPoints.quote: on the record as it exists at that moment

keyPoints.text: The conflict message tells the loser how to keep their work.
keyPoints.quote: it tells the loser what to do with the work they are about to lose

keyPoints.text: The check is the expected() helper in the feedback service.

questions.prompt: Contrast desired-state commands with toggles, and explain the board's rules for deleting, hiding and merging ideas.

keyPoints.text: A command that says enabled: true can be repeated safely and leaves one vote.
keyPoints.quote: Sending it twice should leave one vote.

keyPoints.text: A toggle sent twice by an accidental retry would add and then remove the vote.
keyPoints.quote: would add and then remove the vote

keyPoints.text: This is operation-level idempotency and does not cover post or comment creation.
keyPoints.quote: It does not make post creation or comment creation idempotent

keyPoints.text: An unused open idea can be deleted, but once referenced deletion is rejected and hiding is the workflow.
keyPoints.quote: deletion is rejected and hiding becomes the appropriate workflow

keyPoints.text: A merge keeps the source discussion while moving votes and follows to the canonical target.
keyPoints.quote: A merge retains the original source discussion while moving votes and follows to a canonical target.

keyPoints.text: Visibility stays fixed after creation so old discussions cannot become a privacy trap.
